title: Brothers Robert, Edward, Clarence and Herbert
summary: Hall describes his brothers' instruments and jobs, his singing sister, and a trumpet-playing uncle.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What about Morris French? Did you know him, a trombone player? Morris French? No. He's up around La Posse now, I thought they knew him. What's his name? Morris French. No. He used to work with Louis and Papa Salas. Morris French? No, I don't know him. That's the word before you put about some of your brothers, because most people, you're the famous one, and probably some of your brothers were pretty good too.
Yeah, well I have Mount Woolley's brother, Robert, he was, he was one of them, he was a really good musician. He used to play tenor, played clarinet, I think he played a little piano.
He can do something with a bass, a little trombone, he can do a little everything.
Is he a good get-off man?
Yeah, that's what's good. During those days he used to be playing.
No, I don't think he's playing anymore.
He play every now and then, play ten. Every now and then he get a gig, just play just mostly for kicks. Because he's working for the government now.

Edward is the only one who didn't play anything. Edward didn't play no instrument. But Clarence, Clarence played baritone, I think he played a little Clarence, Herbert, he played Clarence and saxophone. Did you do a sister sing? My sister used to sing. My father was a musician. I had a couple of uncles, a guitar player, and I had one also uncle, a trumpet player. What was his name? Do you remember? His name, uh, Gilles, huh? His nickname was Gilles. We used to call him, his last name was Dewey, huh? We used to call him Piran, I don't know, he's French accent. Dewey?
